about: This piece belongs to the formulary of the First Sunday of Advent, which opens the liturgical year in the 1962 Roman Missal.

s01.translation: To You, O Lord, I lift up my soul. O my God, in You I trust. Let me not be put to shame, nor let my enemies exult over me, for none who await You shall be put to shame.

w013.gloss: may I be put to shame
w013.function: The form is formally either future indicative or present subjunctive. The psalm's parallel future and its petitionary sense do not settle the morphology, so tense and mood are left unclaimed.

w018.function: It matches the plural enemies and means “my”. Reading it as the genitive of the personal pronoun would leave the enemies without the agreement the phrase requires.

w020.function: The adjective stands substantivally for all people. Its relative clause identifies them as those who await the Lord.
